content.text: Section 28 meets the preferred position exactly; no other dispute-resolution provision exists elsewhere in the document.

input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
input.rationale: Section 28 sits at our preferred position: § 28.1 selects New York law, and § 28.2 gives the state and federal courts in New York County exclusive jurisdiction with irrevocable submission and a waiver of venue/forum objections. The only other-court carve-out is the customary one for temporary injunctive relief to protect confidential information or IP, which does not defeat the exclusive merits forum. There is no arbitration clause anywhere in the Agreement, so no offshore seat concern. The § 28.3 pre-filing executive escalation is a fifteen-business-day good-faith step that expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings, and there is no fee-shifting; both are noted only, not deviations.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
mappings.quote: This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.

mappings.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
mappings.quote: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.
